messages:
alyssa: we have a customer hitting lots of 429s during a recent traffic spike. they say requests route between eu-west-1 and us-east-1 and sometimes get cross-region 429s + big latency. any insight?

vikram: can you paste example timestamps + request ids? also which model/version and region preference were they using?

alyssa: sent sample in thread. model: open-llama-13b (redwood-quant v2). customer expects eu-west-1 primarily but we see failover to us-east-1. sample request id: req_0a1b2c3d. timestamps hk: 2026-11-04T15:22:03Z -> 15:22:12Z.

maria: fwiw cross-region failover will try alternate region if capacity breached in primary. but we throttle cross-region at the account level to protect regional capacity — that can produce 429s on the fallback path.

jason: cc @vikram — if the account has per-region quota ceilings, requests that overflow will be rejected at the gateway with a 429 referencing quota_exceeded or cross_region_throttle in the body. usually the error JSON looks like: 
```
{"error":"quota_exceeded","region":"eu-west-1","fallback":"us-east-1","message":"regional capacity exceeded, cross-region routing denied"}
```

alyssa: customer says sometimes the same request succeeds after a few seconds. intermittent. latency spikes from 120ms -> 1.2s when fallback happens.

vikram: that's consistent: fallback routing adds hop + retry window. If fallback is allowed, we attempt L7 routing and may queue briefly; if cross-region throttle blocks, retries fail quickly with 429.

maria: we should check two things: 1) per-account regional capacity and burst window usage during the spike. 2) whether the customer's routing policy allowed fallbacks or pinned to region. ask them to share the request header X-Redwood-Routing and any x-rw-model-version.

alyssa: their header shows: X-Redwood-Routing: prefer=eu-west-1;fallback=auto;max-attempts=2.

jason: with prefer+fallback=auto we try primary then fallback. max-attempts=2 means one retry to fallback. If eu-west-1 was already at reserved capacity but burst exceeded, first attempt returned capacity_error -> then fallback tried but hit cross-region throttle because account-wide cross-region allowance was depleted. Hence 429s on alternate.

maria: repro steps for infra team: simulate sustained burst from a single account to eu-west-1 beyond reserve and observe fallback queue behavior. useful curl: 
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_KEY" 
       -H "X-Redwood-Routing: prefer=eu-west-1;fallback=auto;max-attempts=2" 
       -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","inputs":"test"}' 
       https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
 done
```
watch gateway logs for "cross_region_throttle" and "regional_capacity_exceeded" keys.

vikram: also include the account billing SKU — cross-region routing uses a soft quota based on subscription level; Billing can temporarily block cross-region bursts for some SKUs. @billing-bot can you confirm?

billing-bot: account tier = GrowthMonthly. cross-region burst allowance = 500rps aggregated. current spike peaked at ~860rps across regions for that account during window. billing flags will not block API but quota enforcement is applied by infra layer per policy.

jason: recommendation to customer: 1) pin to eu-west-1 for critical low-latency calls (set fallback=none) or 2) request an increase to regional burst/reserved capacity if they expect sustained traffic. Also add exponential backoff on 429s to avoid thundering.

alyssa: logged repro and assigned to eng-infra. tagging this thread with evidence. customer asked for temporary workaround — how quickly can we change their routing policy?

maria: we can flip routing policy on their account config in console immediately; change takes effect in a minute. to be safe, set fallback=none so no cross-region routing. if they need durability, we can do a short-term reserved capacity bump (support request to sales).

vikram: for eng-infra: please investigate gate metrics: regional_capacity_utilization{region=\"eu-west-1\",account=\"acct-123\"} and cross_region_throttle_count for that account during 2026-11-04T15:20-15:25Z. attach logs and any kube node OOM/eviction events.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-3146, severity=low, owner=eng-infra. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-3146

alyssa: thanks team. I'll send customer the pin-fallback workaround and ETA for infra investigation. keeping thread open until infra posts findings.
